{{Hatnote|Current structure: [[Players Committee organization]]. Changes of advocate are on [[Players Committee advocates]]; the office itself is [[Advocate]].}}
[[File:Players Committee organization chart 2021.png|thumb|right|320px|alt=Players Committee organization chart of 2021|The organization chart of July 2021<ref name="oc2021pdf">PC organization chart PDF (created 8 July 2021), [https://web.archive.org/web/20211005193353/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf archived PDF] (Wayback, 5 October 2021)</ref>]]
Notable changes to the structure of the [[Players Committee]] (PC): its teams, committees and chart.

* '''2002–2003.''' Besides the Advocates, the early swccgpc.com had a Staff Writer, Duane Bruun (Shadow 47),<ref name="pc-jan03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030612020737/http://swccgpc.com:80/Archives/january03archives.htm January 03 Updates], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 12 June 2003.</ref><ref name="pc-bruun02">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030613110815/http://swccgpc.com:80/News/duane2002yearend.htm The State Of SWCCG], Duane Bruun (PC Staff Writer), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 13 June 2003.</ref> and a Championship Circuit Assistant, [[Nick Kolnik]] (April 2003).<ref name="pc-apr03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030810085606/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/april03archives.htm April 03 Updates], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 10 August 2003.</ref> The Advocate Council page of April 2003 gives short biographies and names the subcommittees: [[Jim Colson]] ("40 something", Huntsville, Alabama), Shadow Squadron Leader; [[Andrew Howard]] (19, Chicago), in charge of the Classic Format Subcommittee; [[Eric Olson]] (26, Chicago), manager of the Q&A Subcommittee that proofread the virtual cards; [[Josh Radke]] (23, Bristol, Connecticut); [[Jason Robinette]] (31, New York), head of the Young Jedi Design Subcommittee; and [[Doug Taylor]] (37, Seattle), head of the Proofreading and Public Relations subcommittees and liaison with ''Scrye'' magazine.<ref name="pc-council03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030418002012/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/council.htm Advocate Council] (April 2003), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 18 April 2003.</ref>
* '''June 2003.''' Because Decipher was changing its tournament and ranking software, the PC forms a tournament-software subcommittee with [[Eric Olson]] and [[Andrew Howard]] as project managers; meanwhile tournament directors are asked to register a credit card with Decipher.<ref name="pc-tourchg">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030809102648/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/tournamentchanges06182003.htm Upcoming Changes to Decipher's Tournament Software; How does it affect you?], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 9 August 2003.</ref>
* '''19 April – 19 May 2004.''' The Flight Leader program is announced on 19 April 2004, and the first Flight Leaders are named on 19 May 2004; [[Josh Radke]] becomes the first Kashyyyk Flight Leader.<ref name="pc-int0406">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040602195521/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com news (May 2004)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 2 June 2004.</ref> The Shadow Squadron page of June 2004 lists the regions and their Flight Leaders (see [[SWCCG regions]]).<ref name="pc-vol04">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040604020531/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/volunteers.htm Shadow Squadron (volunteers by region)] (June 2004), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 4 June 2004.</ref>
* '''June 2004.''' A WebGroup is formed to coordinate the PC website: webmaster Keith Allen, with [[Jason Robinette]], [[David Destefanis]], John Davis, [[Kevin Brownell]] and [[Nick Kolnik]].<ref name="webgroup">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040603214022/http://www.swccgpc.com/News/NewAdvocates.htm New Advocates! Not 1 but 2!], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 3 June 2004)</ref>
* '''May 2006.''' The Shadow Squadron is the PC's marketing arm. A Proofreading Subcommittee and a Public Relations Subcommittee are headed by [[Doug Taylor]], and a Young Jedi Design Subcommittee by [[Jason Robinette]].<ref name="adv2006">[https://web.archive.org/web/20060617221233/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=Content&pa=showpage&pid=3 Advocates], swccgpc.com Content pid=3 (published 1 May 2006; Wayback, 17 June 2006)</ref>
* '''March 2008.''' A League program is announced on 19 March 2008: leagues run one qualifying event a month from April to August 2008, and each league champion receives a Day 2 bye; the PC League Coordinator is [[Evan Fitzgerald]].<ref name="pc-sid79">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080712071956/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=79 2008 League Information] (19 March 2008), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 12 July 2008.</ref> On 28 March 2008 [[Michael Erisman]] thanks the Tournament Committee for its update of the Tournament Guidelines.<ref name="pc-sid80">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080712072001/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=80 Changes to the Tournament Guide - Effect 4/1/08] (28 March 2008), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 12 July 2008.</ref>
* '''July 2008.''' The PC announces the first Worldwide SWCCG Day for 26 July 2008, coordinated by Cedric (simone89), who also coordinates the 2008 Canada Nationals.<ref name="pc-sid90">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080803140549/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=90 Worldwide SWCCG Day 2008] (13 July 2008), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 3 August 2008.</ref><ref name="pc-sid91">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080915132734/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=91 Travel Voucher for Canada Nationals 2008] (19 July 2008), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 15 September 2008.</ref>
* '''September 2008.''' Regional Flight Leaders (tournament contacts) and Key Volunteers who lead teams are listed beside the Advocate Council: Website Admin, Moderators, Watto's Cube Team, Player Created Card Team, Proofreading, Graphic Design, Rules Moderators, Competitive Balance Team, Star Wars Information Pool and Tournament Committee.<ref name="vol2008">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080925101022/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/volunteer/ Volunteer], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 25 September 2008)</ref>
* '''July 2009.''' The Volunteer page, now on starwarsccg.org, adds a Premium Member Admin and announces two Flight Leaders per region.<ref name="vol2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102812/http://www.starwarsccg.org/volunteer/ Volunteer], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 6 July 2009)</ref>
* '''June 2018.''' The PC takes over [[GEMP]] from its creator, [[Troy Biesterfeld]], and invites applications for a development team. A new [[Multimedia and Special Projects Advocate]] leads the team.<ref name="gemp2018">[https://web.archive.org/web/20201128163934/https://www.starwarsccg.org/gemp-announcements-request-for-applications-for-new-team/ GEMP Announcements &amp; Request for Applications for New Team], starwarsccg.org (7 June 2018; Wayback, 28 November 2020)</ref>
* '''July 2018.''' Design opens applications for the Design and Development team and the Player Card Development team.<ref name="dd2018">[https://web.archive.org/web/20200927002833/https://www.starwarsccg.org/call-for-applications-dd-team-and-player-card-dev-team/ Call for Applications &ndash; D&amp;D Team and Player Card Dev Team], starwarsccg.org (18 July 2018; Wayback, 27 September 2020)</ref>
* '''December 2020.''' The Jawa Council ([[Kendall Halman]], [[Eric Hunter]] and [[Bill Kafer]]) updates the banned list of the Jawa Format, an alternative format on GEMP.<ref name="jawa">[https://web.archive.org/web/20210125020218/https://www.starwarsccg.org/jawa-format-banned-list-updated/ Jawa Format Banned List Updated!], starwarsccg.org (19 December 2020; Wayback, 25 January 2021)</ref>
* '''January 2021.''' The PC publishes an organization chart under About Us, to be updated every couple of months.<ref name="orgpost">[https://web.archive.org/web/20210130223738/https://www.starwarsccg.org/players-committee-org-chart-published/ Players Committee Org Chart Published!], starwarsccg.org (30 January 2021)</ref> The chart of 14 February 2021 shows Legal and PC Store Manager beside the Lead Advocate.<ref name="oc2021feb">[https://web.archive.org/web/20210214073243/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.jpg PC organization chart], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 14 February 2021)</ref>
* '''March 2021.''' The Competitive Balance Team is announced: 11 members chaired by [[Jarad Konsker]], including several advocates.<ref name="cbt">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/meet-the-competitive-balance-team/ Meet the Competitive Balance Team], starwarsccg.org (25 March 2021)</ref>
* '''July 2021.''' A redesigned chart groups the volunteer teams under labeled sub-teams: GEMP Slicers, Proofing, Playtesting, Player Card Development, Graphics, Competitive Balance Team and Design &amp; Development.<ref name="oc2021pdf" />
* '''May 2024.''' The Technology team moves under the [[Rules Advocate]], and the new [[Production Advocate]] heads Player Card Development and Graphics. The Outreach Team, Stream Team, Decklist Scribe Team and Design Pods are new to the chart.<ref name="oc2024">PC organization chart PDF (created 6 May 2024), [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010210152/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf archived PDF]</ref>
